title: The Predictable Weekly Cadence
overview: Daniel Priestley gave you a one-page marketing strategy you can run as a one-person business: Short Form, Long Form, Lead Form, posted every single day so the new AI-driven recommendation engines can match you with your ideal customers. You learned the two rules of familiarity (11 exposures in 90 days, then 2 to 7 hours of content to earn trust), how to structure the content that does each job, and how to build the product and service ecosystem that turns that attention into revenue, and why, underneath the strategy, the real game is bringing your life force to the people you serve.
key_ideas: Social media has moved from the social graph (your posts go to friends and family) through the interest graph (whatever is trending, like a Ferrari on fire) to the semantic graph, where AI understands what your post is about and matches it to the people who are already interested. Daniel called it a magical telephone and a free call centre: you only need to tell it the problem you solve (your intellectual property or signature method) and who it is for (your ideal customer persona). Short-form video is the frontier model of this technology: YouTube alone serves about 200 billion short videos a day (up from 5 billion a few years ago), roughly 500 billion a day across all platforms, for about 5 billion people with fast internet. You can consume that attention or create with it.

The old formula was product or service, then physical location, then a business brand. All three are weakening: products get compared on price (as airlines did once comparison sites arrived), location no longer limits who you can serve, and business brands get almost no attention online. The new formula is IP + ICP + PSE + Personal Brand: intellectual property, ideal customer persona, product and service ecosystem, and a personal brand that earns the attention. Every Mindvalley teacher you have heard this weekend is running this same formula. A personal brand is about 20 times more powerful than a business brand; posting from a faceless brand is like paying a 95 per cent attention tax. One footballer has more followers than all the football clubs combined, Richard Branson has millions where Virgin has a couple of hundred thousand, and Steven Bartlett has 3 million on LinkedIn versus under 50,000 for Diary of a CEO. People trust the person (Tim Cook), buy the product (iPhone) and commit to the business (Apple), in that order.

Your intellectual property is your baggage: the triumphs and struggles of the last 5 to 10 years. AI can synthesise any textbook or PhD-level research, but it has never lived a day, so your lived stories are the human advantage. You are too close to see the value, like standing on a mountain and being unable to see the mountain. Imperfections are what make people relate, as John Cleese said of great characters.

Two rules to live by. First: people see you for the first time when they see you for the 11th time, and it has to happen within 90 days, so posting once a week is below the minimum effective dose. Post at least once a day, 5 to 7 days a week (Daniel himself aims for about 200 posts a month, 3 to 5 a day, on each platform). Second: people trust you after consuming 2 to 7 hours of your content (drawing on Google's research and Professor Robin Dunbar's work on acquaintance).

Short form (15 to 180 seconds) names your ideal customer, says what you do for them, and rotates through Pain, Prize, Problem, News to stop the scroll, then points to longer content (comment a word, a link in the description, or a short post followed by a 4 to 6 minute video). Instagram, LinkedIn and YouTube are enough to take you to your first 1 to 5 million in revenue.

Long form (6 to 90 minutes) wins trust with Proof, Principles, Process, and switches on the light bulb moments your customer is missing. Climb the podcast pyramid: be a guest on shows under 1,000 views and drive your episode past 1,000, then the 1,000 to 10,000 tier, then 10,000 to 100,000, then 100,000 plus, then a million plus. Daniel has appeared on Diary of a CEO eight times with 40 to 50 million views, and one recent video clocked 46,000 hours of watch time, the equivalent of 20 years of one person's working hours or 20 salespeople working for a year.

Lead form: nobody fills in a form for a stranger, but they will after long-form content. Have at least four ways to engage (contact form, self-assessment or scorecard, workshop registration, a waitlist for something coming, a special offer for something disappearing). Capture NEPAL (name, email, phone, location) plus segmentation data about their current situation, desired outcome, obstacle and preferred solution.

The product and service ecosystem has four parts: a gift (your free long-form content), a product for prospects (an online assessment or a book), a core offer in gold, silver and bronze (done for you, done with you, do it yourself), and a product for clients for the ongoing relationship. Daniel's Key Person of Influence Scorecard was taken by 90,000 people and produced about 20 million dollars in sales; Nora switched her traffic from her core offer to an assessment and made two and a half million pounds in the following months; a 48-question assessment won him a celebrity coaching client with 22 million followers within 48 hours. Gabriela Rosa gave away 1,000, then 2,000, then 4,000 copies of her book Fertility Breakthrough and grew from 700,000 to 4.7 million dollars a year. One client's weekly live Q&A membership at 39 pounds a month with 250 members brings in about 117,000 pounds a year. Zooming out, the industrial age wanted you to be a reliable can opener; the digital age wants your vitality, so be the irreplaceable life force for a specific outcome and community, and be a directionalist, not a perfectionist.

frameworks.name: Short Form, Long Form, Lead Form
steps: Short form (15 to 180 seconds) to get attention: name your ideal customer persona, say what you do for them, and share a pain, a prize, a problem or news; post every day.
Long form (6 to 90 minutes: videos, podcasts, a book) to build trust: deliver Proof, Principles, Process and the light bulb moments your buyer is missing.
Lead form to capture the lead and start the product ladder: a dedicated page whose only job is to get the form filled in.

frameworks.name: The new formula: IP + ICP + PSE + Personal Brand
steps: IP: your intellectual property or signature method, drawn from your lived experience.
ICP: your ideal customer persona, the intended audience.
PSE: your product and service ecosystem, the product ladder that sits underneath the IP and ICP.
Personal brand: where the attention comes from, instead of a business brand.

frameworks.name: 11 Interactions and 7 Hours
steps: People notice you for the first time when they see you for the 11th time, and it must happen within 90 days.
People trust you after consuming 2 to 7 hours of your content.
Build a system that clocks up both so people notice, know and trust you and are ready to engage.

frameworks.name: Pain, Prize, Problem, News
steps: Pain: the frustration or struggle they feel right now.
Prize: the result they want.
Problem: the obstacle that explains why most people do not get the result.
News: what is already trending and being looked at.
Rotate through the four, one post a day.

frameworks.name: Proof, Principles, Process
steps: Proof that you know what you are talking about.
Universal principles they can learn from.
A process for getting the result or working with you.

frameworks.name: The Podcast Pyramid
steps: Guest on small podcasts under 1,000 views and promote your episode past 1,000.
Move up to shows in the 1,000 to 10,000 range and drive your episode past 10,000.
Then 10,000 to 100,000, driving past 100,000.
Then 100,000 plus, then a million plus.

frameworks.name: Lead form data: NEPAL plus segmentation
steps: Contact information: Name, Email, Phone, Location (NEPAL).
Which best describes your current situation?
Which best describes the outcome you want to achieve?
Which best describes the struggle or problem you are trying to overcome?
Which best describes the solution you think would suit you?
Is there anything else you want me to know?

frameworks.name: Four products and services
steps: Gift: free value that gets attention (your long-form content).
Product for prospects: what people fill in the lead form for, ideally an online assessment or a book.
Core offer: your main revenue product, in gold (done for you), silver (done with you) and bronze (do it yourself).
Product for clients: the ongoing relationship, such as a membership or subscription.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Priestley
quotes.text: You just have to talk passionately about the problem that you solve and the intended audience of who it's for, and let AI do the rest.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Priestley
quotes.text: And you're standing on top of a mountain of value, but sometimes you're too close to see it.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Priestley
quotes.text: People see you for the first time when they see you for the 11th time.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Priestley
quotes.text: Don't promote what you do, promote the assessment. That is the product for prospects.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Priestley
quotes.text: The book that changes your life is not one that you read, it's one that you write.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Most experts create content whenever they feel inspired, which means it's inconsistent and it kills your authority. Daniel's going to teach you the weekly system, the repeatable cadence that builds your audience whether you feel like it or not. Please welcome Daniel Priestley.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel Priestley
dialogue.text: Jason, thank you very much for a very wonderful introduction. I spent the last 25 years building and selling companies. I've had seven startups that went zero to a million in the first 12 months, and I've been sharing what I know in books like Key Person of Influence. I want to share with you some of the best thinking I've got right now about what to do in the year ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel Priestley
dialogue.text: Out of curiosity, are you enjoying this? Are you getting key ideas? Let me know in the chat what's been your biggest light bulb moment so far, so I can spend some time on this product and service ecosystem.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel Priestley
dialogue.text: Some of you are feeling a little bit overwhelmed, I can see that. Don't be. I'm giving you a lot, but we've got plenty of time to implement this. When people get overwhelmed, it's because they want it to be done. All you have to do is keep moving in the right direction. Be a directionalist, not a perfectionist.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel Priestley
dialogue.text: If you think it's about short form, long form, lead form, you've actually missed the point. The real reason we do this is life-force energy: to play a bigger game, make a bigger impact and raise the vitality in your community and on the planet. I'll hand back to Jason.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Thank you so much, Daniel. Who here is feeling their life force big time right now? I love that he made that distinction, separating the strategies and practices from the real underlying principle: how do we bring our life force to the world and activate more of it in the people we want to serve?

exercises: This week, spend time pausing, reflecting and documenting your last 5 to 6 years: What is the underlying theme? Why do people come back to you with questions? What do people at a dinner party want to know more about? What problems can you solve easily that others struggle with? Ground every answer in a real story, including the struggles.

Prompt your AI assistant: 'I want to develop some intellectual property that's unique to me. Ideally I will have a signature method and a unique name for what I offer. Based on my story, my experiences, my triumphs and struggles, please ask me questions to help me uncover some potential signature content that's mine.'

Prompt: 'I'm developing some short-form videos to promote my business. Based on what you know about me, help me develop scripts that will engage my perfect clients. I want to hook attention, deliver something of value, and get people to comment a word in exchange for longer, more detailed content. Ask me any clarifying questions, then begin creating short-form video scripts.'

Prompt: 'Based on what you know about my core offer, what are the 10 beliefs someone would have to have in order to enthusiastically buy from me?' Treat those as the 10 light bulbs your long-form content must switch on.

Brand audit prompt: 'Search online for content featuring me. How would AI build an understanding of my current personal brand, in particular my intended audience, my offer, my points of difference, whether I am perceived as a key person of influence, and the total amount of content that can easily be found and consumed?'
Design your assessment: if someone is not sure whether they could get value from you, what 15 or so questions would help them become sure? Then promote the assessment rather than the offer.
next_steps: Commit to one short-form post a day, 5 to 7 days a week, on Instagram, LinkedIn and YouTube, rotating Pain, Prize, Problem, News and ending each with a pointer to longer content.
Record or schedule one piece of long-form content (a 10 to 30 minute step-by-step video, or pitch yourself to a small podcast in your niche) built around Proof, Principles, Process.
Set up at least one lead form this week, ideally a self-assessment scorecard, capturing name, email, phone and location plus the segmentation questions.
Run the four AI prompts above and keep the outputs as the start of your signature method and your brand audit.
attribution_notes: Lines marked 'Mindvalley' are the host Jason Goldberg (Daniel addresses him by name); all other lines are Daniel Priestley, who presented largely uninterrupted and responded to chat reactions rather than spoken questions. There was no live audience Q&A in this recording, so the dialogue consists of the host's introduction and close and Daniel's chat check-ins. Daniel did not present an activity dashboard; the cadence as taught is the daily posting rule and the short form, long form, lead form rhythm captured above. The host's opening housekeeping about the Mastery programme has been left out of these notes as it was not part of Daniel's teaching.
